governingAuthorities.rationale: Directive 2013/34/EU is an EU directive adopted by the Parliament and Council: an enacted legal instrument, not an institution's account of one, which is what separates it from official_body.
Directive (EU) 2022/2464 is an EU directive on the same footing. Most of its content was inserted into 2013/34/EU and is read there; its own Article 5 application timetable was not.
Directive (EU) 2026/470 is an EU directive. Its amendments to 2013/34/EU are read in the host; its own transitional provisions, including the FY2025-26 national relief option, are only here.

Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 is a delegated regulation adopted under Article 29b — binding in its entirety and directly applicable, not guidance about a rule, which is why it is not official_body.

The revised ESRS delegated act, C(2026) 5010, is a Commission delegated regulation. It is not official_body: that tier is for an institution's account of the law, and this is the instrument. Its temporal status is recorded in the pack's sources.json, not here, and does not bear on the tier.

The voluntary-standard delegated act, C(2026) 5011, is a Commission delegated regulation on the same footing as SRC-007, and is the instrument defining the value-chain cap catalogue rather than an explanation of it.

authorisedOrigins.rationale: The Accounting Directive's ELI identifies the instrument, and the documents beneath it are its official expressions — including the consolidated readings the corpus pins. Declared as a prefix rather than exactly because a consolidation carries a date segment the OJ publication does not, and both are the same instrument. Nothing outside this ELI is authorised for SRC-001, so the other EUR-Lex sources on this host confer nothing on it and it confers nothing on them.

The Omnibus is served from its OJ publication and nothing else is authorised for it today. Declared exactly rather than by prefix because no consolidation of this act is pinned: the narrower matcher is the truthful one, and widening it later is a decision to record rather than a default to inherit.

ESRS Set 1 is served from its consolidated expression at 01/01/2025 (CELEX 02023R2772-20250101), and nothing else is authorised for it today. Declared exactly rather than by prefix because that one expression is what the corpus pins, and because it is already current: EUR-Lex dates a consolidation by the date its text applies, and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1416 applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025, so this consolidation carries the amended Annex I rather than lagging it. A later consolidation would be a different expression and a decision to record, not a permission inherited from this one. Note that EUR-Lex also serves this expression under a language-suffixed path ending `/eng`; that is a different path and this declaration does not authorise it, deliberately — the corpus pins the language-neutral consolidation form, as `DOC-32013L0034` does.
